https://www.azernews.az/region/263523.ht.text: Israel Epstein: Jewish journalist who became a Chinese Communist Party insider 7 September 2026 20:00 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more Few journalists in the 20th century had a career as unusual as Israel Epstein: born to Jewish parents in Warsaw, raised in China, a committed Communist, a member of the Chinese Communist Party and eventually one of the country’s most prominent foreign-born political figures. Epstein was born in 1915 in Warsaw and arrived in China with his family when he was just two years old. He grew up in Tianjin and began working as a journalist while still a teenager. During the Second Sino-Japanese War, he reported on China and developed close ties with the Chinese Communist movement. His relationship with the Communist Party deepened after he visited the Communist base at Yan’an, where he reported on Mao Zedong's movement. Chinese state records later described Epstein as a foreign-born Communist who helped bring the party's message to the English-speaking world. Epstein eventually became one of the rare foreign-born members of the Chinese Communist Party. He obtained Chinese citizenship in 1957 and formally joined the CCP in 1964. He later became a member of the Standing Committee of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. His work also put him unusually close to Mao's political project. In the early 1960s, Epstein was part of a team of Chinese and foreign scholars working on English translations and revisions of Mao Zedong's Selected Works. The group included several foreign-born Jewish intellectuals who had committed themselves to the Chinese Communist cause. But Epstein's loyalty to the Communist system did not protect him from the Cultural Revolution. In 1968, during Mao's campaign of political purges, Epstein was arrested on allegations of plotting against Premier Zhou Enlai. He spent several years imprisoned before being released in 1973. According to biographical accounts, Zhou later apologized to him, and Epstein's political privileges were restored. What makes Epstein's story particularly striking is that imprisonment did not lead him to abandon communism. Academic research into his life describes him as a fervent supporter and defender of the Cultural Revolution even after experiencing its repression personally. He remained in China for the rest of his life, continuing to write and participate in political and cultural institutions. In 2005, Chinese President Hu Jintao personally visited him shortly before his death in Beijing at the age of 90. Epstein was buried at the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery, traditionally reserved for prominent figures of the Chinese Communist revolution. The paradox of Israel Epstein is what makes his life so remarkable: a Jewish child born in Warsaw became a Chinese journalist, a Communist Party member, a translator of Mao, a political prisoner during Mao's own Cultural Revolution — and, after surviving that imprisonment, remained a committed Communist until his death. https://www.ziarulprofit.ro/attila-kim-a.text: Share Tweet Architect Attila Kim is the new Commissioner for Romania’s participation in the International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia. „Attila Kim has been appointed by the Minister of Culture, Ioana Ciocan, as Commissioner for Romania’s participation in the 61st edition of the International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia,” the Ministry of Culture announced on Monday in a Facebook post. According to the Ministry of Culture, Attila Kim is one of the most renowned and award-winning architects specializing in the design of art and design exhibitions, having collaborated over the years with numerous galleries and museums in Romania and across Europe. He possesses extensive experience in the design of exhibitions and cultural events, restoration, and architectural projects; he has been nominated four times for the European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture – the Mies van der Rohe Award (2009, 2011, 2017, 2026) and has won numerous national awards at the Bucharest Architecture Biennale, the Bucharest Architecture Annual, the Transylvania Architecture Biennale, and the Arhitext Awards (28 awards and 16 nominations). In 2016, he was honored with the Arts and Society Leadership Award by the Aspen Institute, in recognition of his contributions to Romanian culture, his efforts in promoting Romania internationally, and his support for the development of cultural heritage. Since 2016, Attila Kim has served as the Commissioner for Romania at the Venice Architecture Biennale; he also held this position for the Venice Art Biennale between 2017 and 2022. In 2018, the International Advertising Association nominated him for an Award of Excellence for his role in promoting Romania as a global creative hub. His significant architectural projects – focusing on the design and restoration of buildings dedicated to cultural use – include the Plan B Foundation in Cluj-Napoca, the Art Encounters Foundation in Timisoara, the rehabilitation of the Elvira Popescu Cinema (at the French Institute in Bucharest), and the Arta Cinema in Cluj-Napoca, among various other public buildings designed for cultural and exhibition purposes. His exhibition portfolio includes, among others, ”Picasso en visite” at the new headquarters of the Art Encounters Foundation; the inaugural exhibitions dedicated to artists Victor Brauner and Constantin Brancusi, organized as part of the Timisoara 2023 European Capital of Culture program; Adrian Ghenie: Darwin’s Room at the Venice Biennale; European Travellers: Art from Cluj Today at the Kunsthalle Budapest; and Transformation. Romanian Sculpture – 25 Years After the Revolution at the Beelden aan Zee Museum in The Hague, the Netherlands; as well as the exhibitions Mircea Cantor: Q.E.D., Deimantas Narkevičius: The Cupboard and the Music, Art Education in Bucharest and Romanian Art After 1950, Geta Bratescu: The Artist’s Studio, and the SubREAL retrospective, alongside retrospectives dedicated to artists Stefan Caltia, Liviu Stoicoviciu, Marta Jakobovits, and Peter Jacobi, all of which were held at the National Museum of Contemporary Art. Attila Kim has served as the coordinator and architect for all editions of Romanian Design Week and the Bucharest Design Festival (2013 – present), as well as for several editions of the Diploma festival. Furthermore, he designed the exhibition architecture for various showcases of contemporary Romanian design presented during Stockholm Design Week, Vienna Design Week, Madrid Design Week, London Fashion Week and the London Architecture Festival. He also currently serves as the Commissioner for Romania’s participation in the 20th International Architecture Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia. O monedă a decis cine devine primar Publicat acum 41 de minute la 10 noiembrie 2026 Autor admin Primarul unei mici comunități din Peru a fost ales prin aruncarea unei monede, după ce doi candidați au obținut exact același număr de voturi: 671 fiecare. Voturile au fost renumărate, dar egalitatea a rămas, iar autoritățile electorale au organizat o tragere la sorți publică, permisă de legea peruană. Moneda de un sol a fost în favoarea lui Rubén Quispe Capajaña, care l-a învins astfel pe Salomino Mamani Quispe. Doi candidați au obținut același număr de voturi. Cum a fost decis câștigătorul alegerilor din Peru Situația neobișnuită a avut loc în localitatea Conima, unde alegerile desfășurate pe 4 octombrie s-au încheiat cu o egalitate perfectă între doi candidați, informează Mediafax. Rubén Quispe Capajaña, reprezentant al partidului „Somos Perú”, și Salomino Mamani Quispe, candidat din partea formațiunii „País Para Todos”, au obținut fiecare câte 671 de voturi. Potrivit rezultatelor oficiale furnizate de autoritățile electorale din Peru, ambii candidați au primit 27,7% din voturile valabil exprimate. Voturile au fost numărate de mai multe ori, însă rezultatul a rămas neschimbat. În aceste condiții, autoritățile au decis să aplice procedura prevăzută de legislația peruană pentru situațiile în care doi candidați obțin același număr de voturi. O monedă de un sol a decis cine va conduce comunitatea Pentru stabilirea câștigătorului, Juriul Electoral Special (JEE) din Huancané a organizat o tragere la sorți publică. Un oficial electoral a aruncat în aer o monedă de un sol, iar rezultatul a fost favorabil lui Rubén Quispe Capajaña, reprezentantul partidului „Somos Perú”. Astfel, acesta a devenit câștigătorul alegerilor, învingându-și contracandidatul printr-o procedură neobișnuită, dar permisă de lege.
